Financial figures are from the FY2025 Form 10-K (accession 0001628280-26-003942, filed January 29, 2026); ownership is from the 2026 proxy statement (DEF 14A, accession 0001628280-26-025532, filed April 16, 2026, record date April 1, 2026). OWNERSHIP: the proxy gives Zuckerberg 639,347 Class A shares (marked * for less than 1% of Class A), 341,823,978 Class B shares (99.8% of Class B) and 60.8% of total voting power, but no percentage of all shares, so pctEconomic is null and the 13.49% economic share is in leader.derived (both class counts quoted). Footnote (2): the Class A shares are held by Chan Zuckerberg Biohub, Inc., over which he has sole voting and investment power 'but no pecuniary interest'; the Class B shares are held by the Mark Zuckerberg Trust (3,388,097), CZI Holdings, LLC (109,373,980), Chan Zuckerberg Holdings, LLC (17,061,801), CZI Holdings I, LLC (12,000,000, pledged as collateral for indebtedness), Chan Zuckerberg Holdings II, III, IV and V, LLC (50,000,000 each) and CZ Management, LLC (100). No options or RSUs are included. 5% HOLDERS: the proxy lists only BlackRock (7.2%) and FMR (6.1%), as % of Class A only, and those are the figures recorded; on an all-shares basis they would be lower (Class B is about 13.5% of all shares), and they are not recomputed. Their total-voting-power percentages are 2.8% and 2.4%. Both rest on old Schedule 13G/A filings (BlackRock February 12, 2024), so holder asOf is omitted. Vanguard, listed at 8.5% of Class A in the 2025 proxy, is gone: footnote (21) says its Schedule 13G/A of March 27, 2026 reported no beneficial ownership after an internal realignment on January 12, 2026 under which its subsidiaries report separately, and none of them had filed by the proxy date. CASH: buybacks are cash paid for Class A repurchases in 2025 ($26,248m). Dividends include dividend equivalents on RSUs. GEOGRAPHY: Europe includes Russia and Turkey; Rest of World includes Africa, Latin America and the Middle East (10-K footnote 2); United States alone was $74.78 billion (footnote 1). No employee stock purchase plan appears in the 10-K, so plan is null.
